content.title: USA 2, Dominican Republic 1: How U.S. Advanced to WBC Championship in Thrilling Nail-biter
content.text: Last Update: 03/16/2026 3:19 AM03/16/2026 03:18 amMarch 16, 2026 03:18 UTCUSA advances to World Baseball Classic with epic, drama-filled victory over Dominican RepublicWhat a game.The United States' 2-1 victory over the Dominican Republic in the first World Baseball Classic semifinal was everything a baseball fan would want. Paul Skenes, one of the best pitchers on the planet, spearheaded an incredible group project from Team USA's pitching staff as six pitchers combined to frustrate one of the most formidable lineups ever assembled. Mark DeRosa, much maligned during this tournament, pushed all the right buttons and his move to insert Gunnar Henderson into the lineup yielded half of the American's runs. He also pulled Skenes a bit earlier than some might, immediately bringing about a rally-killing double play. Throw in a few controversial calls that went Team USA's way, Aaron Judge playing incredible defense, Julio Rodriguez's home run-saving catch and there's so much to discuss.The United States will go for their second WBC title on Tuesday night against the winner of Venezuela vs. Italy. If that one is half as good as we saw Sunday night, we're still going to be in for a treat.ByKyle Koster03/16/2026 03:08 amMarch 16, 2026 03:08 UTCFinal: United States 2, Dominican Republic 1Team USA needed everything they had, plus the benefit of a strike three call on a 3-2 pitch to Gerardo Perdomo to end an epic game against the Dominican Republic. Mason Miller's eventful save lifts the Americans into the World Baseball Classic final against the winner of Italy vs. Venezuela. 03/16/2026 03:02 amMarch 16, 2026 03:02 UTCTying run on third with Team USA one out wayMiller got Cruz to ground out to second, advancing Rodriguez to third base. Gerardo Perdomo is the Dominican Republic's last hope one out away from elimination. 03/16/2026 03:00 amMarch 16, 2026 03:00 UTCOneil Cruz pinch-hitting and represents winning runJulio Rodriguez worked a five-pitch walk against Mason Miller to get the tying run on base for the Dominican Republic and advanced to second on the first pitch to pinch-hitter Oneil Cruz. Team USA needs two outs to close the deal. ByKyle Koster03/16/2026 02:54 amMarch 16, 2026 02:54 UTCTeam USA fails to tack on any insurance runsTeam USA will attempt to close out a 2-1 victory after being unsuccessful in multiple attempts to extend their lead. ByKyle Koster03/16/2026 02:45 amMarch 16, 2026 02:45 UTCTeam USA now three outs from World Baseball Classic finalsGarrett Whitlock continued Team USA's stellar night of pitching by getting a 1-2-3 eighth inning to put the Americans even closer to a spot on Tuesday night's finals. Whitlock got struck out Juan Soto and Manny Machado with a weak Vladimir Guerrero Jr. comebacker sandwiched in the middle. ByKyle Koster03/16/2026 02:28 amMarch 16, 2026 02:28 UTCDavid Bednar escapes trouble with back-to-back strikeoutsDavid Bednar flirted with trouble in the seventh inning, surrendering a double to Austin Wells and single to Gerardo Perdomo. But a late jump from Wells kept him from scoring on the latter and after Perdomo stole second base, Bednar struck out Fernando Tatis Jr. and Ketel Marte for the final two outs. Team USA is now just six defensive outs from the WBC finals—and an insurance run or two would go a long way.ByRyan PhillipsAbner Uribe blanks U.S. in the seventhAbner Uribe went quickly through the United States’ lineup in the top of the seventh. The Brewers righty got Pete Crow-Armstrong to fly out to center, then struck out Bobby Witt Jr., and induced a groundout from Bryce Harper. We’re set for a stretch in Miami, the U.S. is holding on.Team USA 2, Dominican Republic 1ByRyan PhillipsBrazobán shuts down U.S.Huascar Brazobán cut right through Team USA’s order in the top of the sixth. He struck out Will Smith, Roman Anthony, and Brice Turang in a row to keep the game tight. The Mets’ reliever struck out the side in a key spot.Team USA 2, Dominican Republic 1ByKyle Koster03/16/2026 01:59 amMarch 16, 2026 01:59 UTCMark DeRosa is pressing all the right buttonsMark DeRosa's decision to bring in Tyler Rogers from the bullpen to face Juan Soto with two runners on and one out in the fifth inning paid off immediately as the reliever was able to induce an 6-3 double play to keep the score 2-1 through five innings. Add this to the decision to start Gunnar Henderson, who got the Americans on the board with a home run, and every new wrinkle has paid off for Team USA's manager.ByRyan PhillipsPaul Skenes leaves in the fifthPaul Skenes is done for the night with one out in the bottom of the fifth. The Pirates ace got a fly out from Geraldo Perdomo to lead off the inning, but an infield single by Fernando Tatis Jr., followed by a hard line drive single to center by Ketel Marte chased him. The reigning NL Cy Young award winner went 4 1/3 innings and allowed one run on six hits, with two strikeouts and no walks. Tyler Rodgers replaces him. Team USA 2, Dominican Republic 1ByRyan PhillipsJulio Rodriguez robs Aaron JudgeAaron Judge isn’t the only outfielder having an outstanding night.Judge came up with one out in the top of the fifth, and blasted a 98 mph fastball from Juan Mejia to deep center field, but Julio Rodriguez wasn’t going to let it leave the park. He leaped at the wall and pulled it back to keep the U.S. lead at one run.Team USA 2, Dominican Republic 1ByRyan PhillipsSkenes escapesAfter loading the bases, Paul Skenes was able to wriggle out of a jam in the fourth inning. He got Austin Wells to fly out to medium-depth left field to end the threat. The U.S. still leads.Team USA 2, Dominican Republic 103/16/2026 01:26 amMarch 16, 2026 01:26 UTCAaron Judge continues to flash the leatherBest known for his bat, Aaron Judge is showing he's a weapon in right field as well. After he recorded an assist to gun down Gerardo Perdomo at third base to end a Dominican Republic rally for the final out of the third inning, Judge made a sliding catch to take away a hit from Juan Soto to begin the fourth. Kyle Koster03/16/2026 01:21 amMarch 16, 2026 01:21 UTCAlbert Pujols forced to make another pitching changeThe Team USA bats have come alive in the top of the fourth inning and it's causing Dominican Republic manager Albert Pujols to dip into his bullpen in quick succession. Luis Severino's scoreless night evaporated with a Gunnar Henderson home run and after Will Smith scorched a lineout to left field, Pujols called in lefty Geogory Soto to face Roman Anthony. Anthony blasted a go-ahead homer and Pete Crow-Armstrong squibbed a comebacker that Soto could not handle. That called for yet another trip to the mound to make a pitching change with Juan Meija trotting in to take the ball. The last move worked out as Meija fanned Bobby Witt Jr. to put an end to the eventful frame.ByRyan PhillipsRoman Anthony goes deep to give Team USA the leadGregory Soto replaced Luis Severino with the game tied and one out in the top of the fourth, and was promptly greeted by a deep home run from Roman Anthony. The Red Sox outfielder worked a 3-2 count, and Soto tried to sneak a 95 mph sinker past him. He failed. Anthony turned it around, blasting the ball 421 feet to center, with an exit velocity of 108.2 mph. The ball was crushed, and the U.S. now has the lead. Team USA 2, Dominican Republic 1ByRyan PhillipsGunnar goes deep to tie it upMark DeRosa looks really smart for adding Gunnar Henderson back into the lineup tonight.With the U.S. down 1-0, Henderson led off the top of the fourth with a solo home run to tie things. In a nine-pitch at-bat that went to a 3-2 count, Henderson got a 95 mph cutter from Luis Severino and launched it 400 feet to deep right center. The ball came off the bat at 105.8 mph. and cleared the wall easily.We’ve got a new ballgame.Team USA 1, Dominican Republic 103/16/2026 01:06 amMarch 16, 2026 01:06 UTCAaron Judge ends rally with rocket throw to third baseSeeking to add to their 1-0 advantage, the Dominican Republic appeared to have something cooking in the fourth inning. With Gerardo Perdomo on first base with two outs, Ketel Marte singled to right field. Perdomo took his chances trying to get to third base but was gunned down thanks to a perfect throw from Aaron Judge. ByRyan PhillipsSeverino works around hits to strike out the sideSeverino struck out Pete Crow-Armstrong to lead off the inning, notching his fourth strikeout in the first trip through Team USA’s lineup. Bobby Witt Jr. then laced a single to left, and Bryce Harper followed by doubling down the right field line. The U.S. had second and third with one out and captain Aaron Judge at the plate. After a good battle, Severino struck Judge out with a 3-2 sweeper. Kyle Schwarber followed Judge and Severino sat him down looking. What an inning for the veteran righty.The U.S. might look back on that inning with a ton of regret.Dominican Republic 1, Team USA 0ByKyle Koster03/16/2026 12:39 amMarch 16, 2026 00:39 UTCDominican Republic takes 1-0 lead on Junior Caminero's record-setting home runPaul Skenes's first mistake of the night was a hanging breaking ball that Junior Caminero deposited over the fence in left field to give the Dominican Republic a 1-0 lead. It's the 15th home run of the World Baseball Classic for the slugging lineup, which sets a new record.ByRyan PhillipsSeverino holds USA scoreless through twoLuis Severino was solid again in the second inning. Will Smith led off with the bloop single to right, but that was all the U.S. would get. Severino struck Roman Anthony out looking on a 99 mph fastball. Then Brice Turang hammered a 96 mph cutter right to second baseman Ketel Marte, who started a double play. The ball came off Turang’s bat at 110.4 mph, but was hit right at Marte for an easy, inning-ending double play.ByKyle Koster03/16/2026 12:28 amMarch 16, 2026 00:28 UTCPaul Skenes finds three quick outs for Team USATeam USA starter Paul Skenes knows he'll have to be efficient tonight against the Dominican Republic with a pitch count in mind and manager Mark DeRosa signaling that he may go on the conservatives side of that benchmark. By that standpoint his first inning couldn't have gone better as Skenes got Fernando Tatis Jr. and Ketel Marte to lift lazy popups and retired Juan Soto thanks to a fine diving play by Brice Turang. In all, Skenes threw nine pitches in the frame. ByRyan PhillipsLuis Severino works a scoreless firstLuis Severino was fired up in the first inning as he ran his fastball up to 99 mph on several occasions. He struck out Bobby Witt Jr. and Bryce Harper swinging, then allowed a single to Aaron Judge, and hit Kyle Schwarber. With the pressure mounting, he got Gunnar Henderson to ground out to second to end the threat. The D.R. is up to bat for the first time. Team USA 0, Dominican Republic 0ByRyan PhillipsOrtiz picks the Dominican RepublicDuring Fox’s pregame show, David Ortiz picked his native Dominican Republic to beat the U.S. and put a little sauce on the prediction. ByRyan Phillips03/16/2026 12:00 amMarch 16, 2026 00:00 UTCBryce Harper visits with Fox studio crewBefore the game started, Bryce Harper stopped by Fox’s studio desk to say hi to Derek Jeter, David Ortiz, and the rest of the crew. ByRyan Phillips03/15/2026 11:53 pmMarch 15, 2026 23:53 UTCFernando Tatis Jr. is ready to face Team USAFox’s Ken Rosenthal caught up with Fernando Tatis Jr. before the game and he predicted the matchup with Team USA would be a dog fight.ByRyan Phillips03/15/2026 10:23 pmMarch 15, 2026 22:23 UTCYankees catcher Austin Wells is a key piece for the D.R.New York Yankees catcher Austin Wells has surprised some people by popping up on the Dominican Republic’s roster. Here’s a full explainer on why he’s playing for the D.R.Despite being born in Scottsdale, Arizona, Wells is of Dominican descent. ByRyan Phillips03/15/2026 10:20 pmMarch 15, 2026 22:20 UTCTeam USA vs. Dominican Republic broadcast informationIf you’re looking to watch Team USA’s matchup with the Dominican Republic in the semifinals of the 2026 World Baseball Classic, we’ve got you covered below.Time: 8 p.m. ETLocation: loanDepot Park, MiamiBroadcast: FS1Announcers: Joe Davis, John Smoltz, Ken RosenthalByRyan Phillips03/15/2026 10:04 pmMarch 15, 2026 22:04 UTCDominican Republic lineup remains potentThe Dominican Republic has had the best offense throughout the 2026 World Baseball Classic. The team leads the tournament in runs scored (51), home runs (14), batting average (.312), on-base percentage (.453), slugging (.637), and OPS (1.090).Here’s how the Dominicans will line up against Paul Skenes and Team USA:Fernando Tatis Jr., RFKetel Marte, 2BJuan Soto, LFVladimir Guerrero Jr., 1BManny Machado, 3BJunior Caminero, DHJulio Rodriguez, CFAustin Wells, CGeraldo Perdomo, SSStarting pitcher: Luis SeverinoByRyan Phillips03/15/2026 10:00 pmMarch 15, 2026 22:00 UTCTeam USA switches up lineup for matchup with Dominican RepublicTeam USA’s manager, Mark DeRosa, is changing up the lineup for his team’s semifinal matchup with the Dominican Republic.
